source.manualTitle: Whirlpool & Maytag 27 in Front-Load Gas & Electric Dryers Service Manual

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dryer or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before accessing.

steps.title: Continue procedure
steps.body: Service Diagnostics entered. Use Key Activation, fault scroll, or Service Test as needed, then continue below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: After diagnostic entry, proceed with OEM component test steps.

steps.title: Service Diagnostic L1/L2 quick check
steps.body: Enter Service Diagnostic Mode. Verify L1 and L2 present at heater relay — confirms centrifugal switch, element, high-limit, and cut-off path.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Enter Service Diagnostic Mode. Verify L1 and L2 present at heater relay — confirms centrifugal switch, element, high-limit, and cut-off path.

steps.title: Access thermal components
steps.body: Remove front panel. Power off before resistance checks.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove front panel. Power off before resistance checks.

images.caption: Heater, hi-limit, and thermal cutoff — electric (W11737351 p.15)

steps.title: Thermal cut-off to heater (~10 Ω)
steps.body: Ohmmeter: red at thermal cut-off to red/white at heater. Expect about 10 Ω. Open → check cut-off, high-limit, and element per strip circuit.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Ohmmeter: red at thermal cut-off to red/white at heater. Expect about 10 Ω. Open → check cut-off, high-limit, and element per strip circuit.

branches.label: No / failed
branches.oemOutcome: Replace open element or cut-off/high-limit pair.

steps.title: Outlet thermistor J14-3 to J14-6
steps.body: Disconnect J14. Use outlet thermistor R/T table. Open/short → replace thermistor or repair harness.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect J14. Use outlet thermistor R/T table. Open/short → replace thermistor or repair harness.

steps.title: L2 / centrifugal follow-up
steps.body: If L2 missing in service mode but element path OK, inspect centrifugal switch before replacing ACU.
steps.sourceExcerpt: If L2 missing in service mode but element path OK, inspect centrifugal switch before replacing ACU.

steps.title: Replace heat components
steps.oemOutcome: Replace failed element, thermal cut-off, and/or high-limit thermostat.

steps.title: Heater circuit verified
steps.oemOutcome: Element path, limits, and outlet NTC within spec.
